text: Meet Satbir, a farmer in Patran. Last November, a fire on the next field went on his record, and the money promised for not burning came months late. Every November, burnt paddy straw from Punjab and Haryana chokes Delhi. Saakshi fixes how farmers are checked, and how they are paid.

This is where Satbir farms, on the Patiala–Kaithal border, through the 2025 season. Red is ground that turned black after harvest, seen by Sentinel-2. Yellow rings are NASA fire alerts. Most burns never raised one. On fields we labelled by hand, fire alerts wrongly flagged nine in a hundred clean fields. Saakshi, fewer than one.

Open any field, and run the check. It reads every clear Sentinel-2 picture of the field, from AWS Open Data, on AWS Lambda. This one, Baljeet's, turned near-black on the sixth of November. A possible burn, and the smoke it released.

Saakshi never punishes on its own. Every possible burn goes to the village officer, with the pictures, the plant signal, and last season's record. When the officer confirms a burn, Saakshi drafts the recovery notice, and sends a link to return the advance.

Satbir's case. A fire alert came from the next field, but his own field shows no burn. The officer approves, and the money goes straight to his bank, through Cashfree Payouts, with a payment advice. Clean fields are paid automatically.
Satbir sees the same pictures, in Punjabi, Hindi, Haryanvi, or English. Hears a voice note. Tracks every rupee. And can appeal, in one tap.

Most farmers live on WhatsApp, so Saakshi does too. Pick, or simply say your name. Your status arrives in English and your own language, with a voice note. Tap Why for the satellite pictures, My money for your balance, or ask by voice, in Punjabi.

All of it runs on AWS. Lambda reads Sentinel-2 in place. DynamoDB keeps every decision, and its audit trail. CloudFront serves the app. And Amazon Bedrock, with the Strands Agents SDK, understands the farmer. The model picks a tool. It never decides.
Paid before harvest. Every field checked. Every burn, confirmed by a person. About nineteen kilograms of PM2.5 kept out of the air, for every acre that stays clean. This is Saakshi.
